solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Say money changing's substantial

parts.note: forex is short for foreign exchange, the trade of changing money
ample means plentiful or substantial

explanation.surface: A remark that currency exchange is a big business.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', joining the wordplay to the opening definition.
explanation.definitionFit: 'Say' used to introduce an instance, as in 'say, a cat', means the same as giving an illustration.

clue.text: Frozen veteran standing outside new house

indicators.note: one word standing outside others surrounds them, so the first word wraps the next pair

parts.note: a veteran is old
N is the abbreviation for new
HO is the abbreviation for house

explanation.surface: An old soldier stands in the cold outside a newly built home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Veteran' here is the adjective old, not a former soldier; HO for house is a standard abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A project that is frozen is suspended, temporarily halted and waiting.

clue.text: Tax collector's old name, as written up

parts.note: ex- means former, old

indicators.note: in a down entry, going up means reading the letters from the bottom, so backwards

parts.note: taken as written
sic is the Latin tag meaning 'thus', used to show something is reproduced exactly as written

explanation.surface: A historical note on what a taxman used to be called, as spelt in the records.
explanation.walkthrough: Only 'name, as written' goes up; EX stays in front. The 's is 'has', a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An exciseman was an officer collecting excise duties, a historic British tax official.

clue.text: Top ten record, one from the bottom

indicators.note: in a down entry, reading from the bottom upwards runs the letters backwards

parts.note: X is the Roman numeral for ten
an EP is an extended-play record
a means one

explanation.surface: A record has crept into the Top Ten, rising from the lowest place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Top ten record' reads like the charts, but Top is the definition and ten is just X.
explanation.definitionFit: The apex of something is its highest point, its peak or top.

clue.text: Fourth or fifth, maybe, or the best of the rest?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: in music, fourths, fifths and octaves are the intervals called perfect
second meaning, playful: a flawless break, perfect being best and an interval a rest

explanation.surface: Fourth or fifth place, or top of the also-rans, as in a race result.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests finishing positions; the first part is music theory, and the second reads the two words literally with a question mark flagging the whimsy.
explanation.definitionFit: Perfect fourths and fifths are named intervals in music theory; a best possible rest is an ideal pause.

clue.text: Drove home, reduced speed in seaside resort

indicators.note: one piece placed in another sits inside it
read as re-sort, to sort again, so the letters are put in a new order

parts.note: taken as written, ready to be rearranged
miles per hour, a speed unit cut down to its abbreviation

explanation.surface: Someone drove home slowly through a holiday town by the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Seaside resort' looks like one phrase but resort is the instruction; 'Drove home' means stressed a point, not a car journey.
explanation.definitionFit: To drive a point home is to press it hard, to stress it.

clue.text: Composer's time to leave group

indicators.note: something told to leave departs, so it is taken out of the word

parts.note: a batch is a group
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A band's composer decides it is time to quit.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is': the composer is BATCH with T removed.
explanation.definitionFit: Johann Sebastian Bach is the German baroque composer.

clue.text: US city needs no more curry

indicators.note: needing none of a word means doing without it, so those letters are dropped

parts.note: the port city in Maryland
taken as written; this is the part removed

explanation.surface: An American city is full and wants no more curry houses.
explanation.walkthrough: BALTIMORE neatly ends in MORE, which goes.
explanation.definitionFit: A balti is a style of curry cooked and served in a metal bowl, popular in Birmingham.

clue.text: Hot air from hand on mouth

parts.note: to give someone a hand is to applaud, to clap
trap is slang for mouth, as in 'shut your trap'

explanation.surface: Breath escaping past a hand held over the mouth.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'on' means placed above, so the first piece sits over the second.
explanation.definitionFit: Claptrap is pretentious, empty talk, which is what hot air means figuratively.

clue.text: Result of punching farmer? Split fences

indicators.note: fences enclose land, so the word given by 'Split' surrounds the other piece

parts.note: to split is to tear
a hick is a rustic, a country farmer

explanation.surface: A farmer is punched; there's a fight over who split the fences.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Split fences' looks like a farm repair job, but Split is the outer word and fences means encloses.
explanation.definitionFit: A thick ear is a swollen ear from a blow, the classic outcome of being hit.

clue.text: Level crossing I'll support

indicators.note: a word crossing another spans it, holding the other inside from end to end

parts.note: on a par means level
I'll with the apostrophe dropped

explanation.surface: Someone backs the building of a level crossing over the railway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Level crossing' is a railway term in the surface; here they are two separate pieces of wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A pillar is a column that holds up a structure, a support.

clue.text: With luxury, no husband needed

indicators.note: 'no' here says the following item is absent, so it is taken away

parts.note: plush means luxurious; luxury used attributively
H is the abbreviation for husband

explanation.surface: A life of luxury: who needs a husband?
explanation.walkthrough: PLUSH loses its final H.
explanation.definitionFit: Plus as a preposition means with or in addition to, as in 'tea plus cake'.

clue.text: I came back and consumed waste

indicators.note: going back means travelling the opposite way, so the letters are read right to left

parts.note: the two words run backwards
consumed food means ate

explanation.surface: I returned and ate up all the leftovers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Waste' looks like a noun for leftovers but is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To emaciate is to make or become very thin, to waste away.

clue.text: Eucharist disrupted quiet clergyman's office once

indicators.note: something disrupted is thrown out of order, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
p (piano) is the musical mark for quiet

explanation.surface: A service was disrupted, upsetting a quiet clergyman's work.
explanation.walkthrough: Both pieces go into the mix together.
explanation.definitionFit: A curateship was the post of a curate, an assistant cleric; 'once' marks the term as dated.

clue.text: One can deal with raised levels of exposure, surely?

definitions.text: One can deal with raised levels of exposure, surely?

parts.note: surface reading: someone resilient to heightened exposure, say to radiation or risk

parts.words: One can deal with raised levels of exposure
parts.note: setter's reading: an animal at home on high, exposed rock ledges

explanation.surface: Someone claims to handle elevated radiation or risk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Raised levels' means high places and 'exposure' means being out on bare crags; the question mark flags the pun.
explanation.definitionFit: This sure-footed wild climber lives on steep, exposed slopes at high altitude.

clue.text: Wind, mostly commonplace, is causing illness

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the final letter is cut

parts.note: wind in the stomach is gas
trite means hackneyed, commonplace
taken as written

explanation.surface: Trapped wind is a common cause of illness.
explanation.walkthrough: Wind fits the stomach theme of the answer neatly.
explanation.definitionFit: Gastritis is inflammation of the stomach lining, a medical condition.

clue.text: Party people are present

parts.note: a do is a party
a nation is a people

explanation.surface: Partygoers are all in attendance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Present' reads as an adjective (here) but is the noun, a gift.
explanation.definitionFit: A donation is a gift, something given, so a present.

clue.text: Well-equipped writers

parts.note: surface reading: authors with all the kit they need
setter's reading: implements each supplied with its own well, an ink reservoir

explanation.walkthrough: 'Well-equipped' means fitted with a well, the reservoir that holds ink; the writers are instruments, not people.
explanation.definitionFit: These pens draw ink from an internal reservoir rather than being dipped.

clue.text: Over a cold, cold sea

parts.note: taken as written
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on a tap
the Ross Sea is a bay of the Southern Ocean off Antarctica

explanation.surface: A sailing trip over an icy sea.
explanation.walkthrough: The second 'cold' belongs with sea: an Antarctic sea is about as cold as they come.
explanation.definitionFit: Across and over both mean from one side to the other, as in 'swam over/across the river'.

clue.text: Scratch plain fabric

parts.note: scratch is slang for money
mere means plain, nothing more than

explanation.surface: Plain cloth that scratches the skin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scratch' looks like a verb about itchy cloth but is slang for money.
explanation.definitionFit: Cashmere is fine soft wool from Kashmir goats, a luxury textile.

clue.text: Quick way to get into bed?

indicators.note: a piece that gets into another ends up inside it

parts.note: hay is bed, as in 'hit the hay'
ST, street, is a way

explanation.surface: Asking for the fastest route into bed.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that bed is hay, the old straw bedding.
explanation.definitionFit: Hasty means done in a hurry, quick.

clue.text: Mass brawl

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a crowd, the common herd
second meaning: a scuffle, as in rugby when players pile in

explanation.surface: A huge free-for-all fight.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both an undistinguished mass of people and a rough tussle or scrum.

clue.text: Cracking sound you'll hear

indicators.note: what you will hear is a word spoken out loud, so we go by its pronunciation

parts.note: to sound water is to plumb it, measuring its depth with a weighted line

explanation.surface: A cracking noise you'll hear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cracking sound' looks like one noise; cracking is the definition (excellent) and sound means measure depth.
explanation.definitionFit: Plum as an adjective means excellent or desirable, as in a plum job, like cracking.

clue.text: Tasteless gear's given award

parts.note: kit is equipment, gear
the possessive ending kept
CH is the Companion of Honour, a British honour

explanation.surface: Somebody's gaudy outfit wins a prize.
explanation.walkthrough: CH, Companion of Honour, is an order awarded by the British monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: Kitsch describes art or objects in poor, showy taste, so tasteless works as the adjective.

clue.text: Will jump to avoid sword pinning one with one leg

indicators.note: pinning something holds it fast within, so the first piece surrounds the next

parts.note: in fencing, a volt is a leap aside to avoid a thrust
I is the Roman numeral one
I is the Roman numeral one again
in cricket the leg side is also called the on side

explanation.surface: A fencer leaps clear of a blade, pinning an opponent while standing on one leg.
explanation.walkthrough: A volt is a fencing term. In cricket, the leg side of the field is also called the on side.
explanation.definitionFit: Volition is the faculty of choosing, the exercise of the will.

clue.text: Just about to have lavatory emptied

parts.note: on means about, concerning

indicators.note: an emptied word has lost its contents, leaving just the outside letters

parts.note: the first and last letters stay, the middle goes

explanation.surface: Just about to have the toilet cleared out.
explanation.definitionFit: Only and just both mean merely or no more than.

clue.text: Faceless spy in old document, rewritten

indicators.note: one piece placed in another sits inside it

parts.note: past means old, former

indicators.note: with no face, the front is gone, so the first letter is removed

parts.note: to spy something is to glimpse it

explanation.surface: A spy hides inside an old document, which gets rewritten.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old document' looks like the definition, but old belongs to the wordplay; the definition is the rewritten document.
explanation.definitionFit: A palimpsest is a manuscript scraped and reused, with fresh writing over faint older text.
